risk_register.description: If team lacks direct experience with the chosen API gateway framework (Kong, AWS API Gateway, Envoy, Spring Cloud Gateway), then development velocity will be 30–50% slower, timeline will slip by 4–6 weeks, and gateway architecture may require rework.
risk_register.trigger: Brief states 'technology_stack: null' and 'team_composition: 4 engineers (no roles, seniority, or stack experience specified)'; open question #1 confirms uncertainty about gateway framework experience.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct technology stack selection workshop in week 1; assign one engineer to spike on chosen framework for 3 days; document gateway architecture patterns and team capability gaps before Phase 2 kickoff.
risk_register.contingency: If velocity drops below 60% of estimate by end of Phase 1, escalate to sponsor; consider hiring external gateway specialist or extending timeline by 4 weeks.

risk_register.description: If authentication service (SSO, OAuth2, API keys, mTLS) is not production-ready, documented, or team lacks integration experience, then gateway cannot enforce consistent authentication; project scope expands or launch is blocked by 2–4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Brief states 'Authentication service integration scope and SLA are defined and available' as assumption A1 with 'risk_if_wrong: HIGH'; open question #2 explicitly flags this as unresolved before build.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm auth service production readiness and API documentation in week 1; schedule 2-day integration spike with auth service team; document auth flow and error handling before Phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If auth service is not ready by end of Phase 1, implement temporary API key authentication in gateway; defer SSO/OAuth2 integration to Phase 2 post-launch.

risk_register.description: If microservice inventory, endpoint contracts, and API documentation are incomplete or undiscovered services emerge mid-project, then gateway routing rules will be incomplete at launch; post-launch service onboarding requires continuous re-scoping and 1–2 week delays per service cluster.
risk_register.trigger: Assumption A2 states 'risk_if_wrong: MEDIUM' but brief explicitly lists 'Multiple services with inconsistent APIs' as trigger; open question #3 confirms microservice inventory is not finalized; brief does not state all services are documented.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct service discovery audit in week 1; document all microservices, endpoint contracts, and current API versions in a shared registry; establish service onboarding checklist before Phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If undocumented services are discovered during Phase 2, add them to backlog as post-launch work; do not block gateway launch; implement service discovery mechanism in gateway to auto-detect new services.

risk_register.description: If team size of 4 engineers is shared across other projects or roles are not clearly assigned (backend developer, integration specialist, QA, product manager), then critical path tasks will slip due to context switching and lack of dedicated ownership.
risk_register.trigger: Brief states 'team_size: 4' and 'team_composition: 4 engineers (no roles, seniority, or stack experience specified)'; project plan states 'Backend Developer and Integration Specialist must be dedicated (not shared)' but brief does not confirm dedication.
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from sponsor that all 4 engineers are 100% dedicated to this project for 17.4 weeks; assign explicit roles (backend lead, integration specialist, QA lead, product manager) in week 1; establish no-context-switching policy.
risk_register.contingency: If any engineer is pulled to other projects, escalate immediately to sponsor; hire contractor to backfill; do not proceed with Phase 2 until full team dedication is confirmed.

risk_register.description: If Product Owner is not assigned or available for timely backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions between rate limiting, versioning, and load balancing features, then feature prioritization will stall and team will build all features equally, risking timeline slip if scope must be cut.
risk_register.trigger: Open question #4 explicitly states 'Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions?' indicating PO role is not assigned; brief does not name a PO or decision-maker.
risk_register.mitigation: Assign Product Owner and confirm 50% allocation minimum in week 1; establish weekly backlog refinement cadence; document feature priority matrix (MVP vs. Phase 2) before Phase 2 kickoff.
risk_register.contingency: If PO is unavailable, escalate to sponsor for interim decision-maker; implement feature freeze at end of Phase 1 to prevent mid-project scope creep.

risk_register.description: If regulatory or compliance requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) exist but are not discovered until Phase 2, then logging architecture must be re-designed to include encryption, PII redaction, and longer retention; 1–2 week delay and potential re-budgeting.
risk_register.trigger: Assumption A3 states 'risk_if_wrong: MEDIUM' and brief explicitly lists compliance as open question #5; brief states 'compliance: null' but does not confirm absence of regulatory requirements.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct compliance requirements discovery in week 1; confirm with legal/security whether SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, or GDPR apply; document logging architecture requirements before Phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If compliance requirements are discovered in Phase 2, implement logging pipeline with encryption and PII redaction; extend timeline by 1–2 weeks; re-budget infrastructure costs.

risk_register.description: If external dependencies (authentication service, logging service, microservices) have undocumented APIs, rate limits, or SLAs, then gateway integration will require additional discovery and testing; 1–2 week delay per dependency.
risk_register.trigger: Brief lists 'external service integration points (microservices, auth service, logging service) are not fully detailed'; use case model identifies 3 external actors (A3, A4, A5) with no SLA or documentation confirmation.
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule integration discovery sessions with each external service owner in week 1; document API contracts, rate limits, SLAs, and error handling; create integration test plan before Phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If external service documentation is incomplete, implement adapter layer in gateway to handle undocumented behavior; add integration testing buffer (1 week) to Phase 3.

risk_register.description: If load balancing strategy (stateless round-robin vs. stateful session affinity) is not confirmed before build, then gateway architecture may require rework if services require session affinity or sticky sessions; 1 week additional development.
risk_register.trigger: Assumption A4 states 'risk_if_wrong: LOW' but brief does not confirm load balancing requirements; use case UC5 (Load Balance Requests) is in scope but strategy is undefined.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm load balancing requirements with microservice owners in week 1; document whether stateless round-robin or stateful session affinity is required; design gateway load balancing layer accordingly.
risk_register.contingency: If stateful routing is required mid-project, implement session affinity in gateway; add 1 week to Phase 2 for distributed state management design and testing.

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 discovery (technology stack, auth service readiness, microservice inventory, compliance requirements) is not completed by end of week 2, then Phase 2 architecture and build will be delayed; timeline slip of 1–2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Brief lists 5 open questions marked 'Before build' with 'urgency: Before build'; brief does not confirm discovery is complete; project plan assumes Phase 1 is 2 weeks but discovery scope is not finalized.
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate 2 full weeks to Phase 1 discovery; assign one engineer to lead discovery; create discovery checklist covering all 5 open questions; schedule gate review at end of week 2 before Phase 2 kickoff.
risk_register.contingency: If discovery is incomplete by end of week 2, extend Phase 1 by 1 week; do not start Phase 2 architecture until all open questions are resolved.

risk_register.description: If API versioning strategy (header-based, path-based, or content negotiation) is not defined before build, then gateway routing logic will require rework; 1 week additional development and testing.
risk_register.trigger: Use case UC6 (Support API Versioning) is in scope but brief does not specify versioning strategy; brief does not confirm how microservices currently handle versioning.
risk_register.mitigation: Define API versioning strategy in Phase 1 discovery; document routing rules for each version; create versioning test plan before Phase 2 build.
risk_register.contingency: If versioning strategy changes mid-project, implement versioning adapter in gateway; add 1 week to Phase 2 for re-testing.
